problem:
A checkpoint can be used once, by the agent that wrote it, to continue the conversation it came from:
- Cutting over is bound to the checkpoint's own conversation and agent (hub/hub/checkpoint_cutover.py:170-174). It archives the original (conversations.py:531-534).
- It is refused once that conversation has been handed over: a conditional update plus a unique index of one handover per conversation (models.py:2327-2335).
- The Checkpoints page lists and reads every checkpoint, but its detail view has no action (hub/ui/src/components/checkpoints/CheckpointsPage.tsx:140-222). The only cut-over button is in the conversation panel, and only for an offered checkpoint (AgentOutputPanel.tsx:751-800).

So the operator cannot:
- go back to an earlier point in a line of work and try again from there;
- hand a well-summarised state to a different agent, for example a cheaper model or a reviewer;
- start a second attempt alongside the first.

Each of those today means copying a checkpoint's text into a new conversation by hand.

requirements.statement: The operator can start a new conversation from any checkpoint of the project that was written, whatever its age, its trigger, and whether it has already been carried over or used to start other conversations.

requirements.rationale: The point of choosing another agent is often a different model or role; inheriting the original's overrides would quietly undo the choice.
requirements.statement: When starting, the operator chooses the conversation's agent from the project's open agents, with the checkpoint's own agent offered first; the new conversation belongs to that agent and runs with that agent's own runner, model and permissions, not the original conversation's overrides.

requirements.rationale: A checkpoint is written in the first person of the agent that produced it (it lists 'every task assigned to this agent'); read unannotated by another agent, it would be taken as that agent's own state.
requirements.statement: The new conversation's first input is the checkpoint, rendered as a carry-over renders it. When the chosen agent is not the checkpoint's own, the input first says whose conversation the checkpoint was written in, and that the tasks it lists are that agent's, not the reader's.
When starting, the operator may add a message of their own, which is delivered after the checkpoint in the same first turn.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-06. Unlike an automatic carry-over, this is a deliberate operator action, so a second confirmation adds a click and nothing else.
requirements.statement: The new conversation's first turn starts as soon as the operator confirms, without a separate Continue, whatever the project's carry-over setting says.

Starting from a checkpoint changes nothing about the conversation the checkpoint came from or about the checkpoint itself: the conversation stays open or archived as it was, its runs and queue are untouched, and a checkpoint not yet carried over can still be carried over afterwards.

requirements.rationale: Without the record, a second attempt is indistinguishable from fresh work, and the Checkpoints page's lineage would show only the carry-over.
requirements.statement: A conversation started this way records the checkpoint it started from. The conversation shows it, with a link to that checkpoint, and the checkpoint lists every conversation started from it, each with its agent and when, apart from the conversation it was carried into.
The new conversation is titled from the checkpoint's title, marked as started from a checkpoint, and the operator can rename it.

requirements.rationale: The operator can already read every checkpoint, and here they choose what to hand over. A grant check would make the operator ask permission of their own setting.
requirements.statement: Starting another agent from a checkpoint needs no checkpoint-reading grant for that agent; the grant continues to govern only what an agent may read with its own tools.

Starting is refused, saying why, when the checkpoint was never written, when the chosen agent is archived or not in this project, or when the checkpoint belongs to another project; a refused start creates no conversation.

in_scope: A start action on any written checkpoint in the Checkpoints page, with a choice of agent
The new conversation: its agent, its first input, its title, and its record of the checkpoint it started from
Showing, on a checkpoint, the conversations started from it, and on a conversation, the checkpoint it started from
Leaving the original conversation and the checkpoint's carry-over untouched
non_goals: A start action anywhere but the Checkpoints page, such as the conversation view (operator, 2026-11-06)
Changing how the automatic or offered carry-over works, including that it archives the original
Editing a checkpoint's text before starting from it
Starting from a checkpoint of another project
Agents starting conversations from checkpoints themselves (an MCP tool)
Starting from a checkpoint that was never written (unwritten or failed)
Merging two conversations, or carrying a conversation's provider session over

summary: From the Checkpoints page, the operator picks any written checkpoint, including an old one or one already carried over, chooses any agent of the project, and starts a new conversation for that agent whose first input is that checkpoint. Its first turn starts as soon as the operator confirms. The original conversation, and the checkpoint's own carry-over, are left exactly as they were. One checkpoint can start any number of conversations, and each one records where it started from.
